title: Collaboration between parents and nurses in the pediatric care process – a pilot interview study
summary:
This study focuses on the collaboration between nurses and parents whose children are receiving inpatient care in a hospital setting. Previous research suggests that nurses do not always view parents as a resource to be actively involved in the care process. This contrasts with the principles of family-centered care, in which parents are considered a valuable resource and an integral part of the children´s care during hospitalization.
The aim of the study is to deepen the understanding of collaboration between nurses and parents in order to promote the implementation of family-centered care. To achieve this, individual interviews will be conducted with both groups. These interviews will explore their experiences, perspectives and expectations. The insights gained are intended to support targeted improvements in everyday nursing practice and strengthen effective cooperation.
conditions: Collaboration between nursing professionals and parents of pediatric patients

interventions.name: Parents accompanying their children who have been admitted to hospital as inpatients
Nursing staff in pediatric peripheral wards

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Parents of hospitalized patients
•	Minimum age: 18 years
•	Willingness and informed consent to participate in the interview
•	Good knowledge of German 
•	Criteria for patient selection:- Minimum hospital stay of 72 hours, - Admission of an accompanying person, - Age ≤ 9 years

Nursing professionals
•	Minimum age: 18 years
•	Willingness and informed consent to participate in the interview
•	The nurse, who was responsible for the nursing process, cared for the selected patient during at least two shifts
•	Good knowledge of German 
•	Licensed/qualified nurse (or equivalent professional qualification, regardless of job title)
Exclusion criteria:
•	Lack of informed consent to participate in the study
•	Language barriers
•	Parents of patients:- In life-threatening or critical situations (e.g., terminal patients, newly diagnosed chronic conditions), - With unstable health conditions
•	Nursing professionals: - Close personal relationship to the researcher, - Nursing professionals currently in the process of professional recognition (validation of qualifications)
